l4_steps.name: Extract fuel volume forecast from flight schedule
l4_steps.input: Approved flight schedule (SSIM), fleet assignment by station
l4_steps.output: Station-level fuel volume forecast (US gallons by month, 12-month horizon)
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥95% vs actual uplift volume at month-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Schedule changes post-freeze invalidate fuel pre-purchases with no automated re-forecast trigger in SkyWORKS; manual rework required for each schedule revision

l4_steps.name: Model price scenarios and set hedging target
l4_steps.input: Fuel volume forecast, Platts jet fuel spot prices, 12-month forward curve
l4_steps.output: Hedge ratio recommendation (% of forward volume), scenario P&L analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Hedge ratio within board-approved policy band of 30–70% of forward 12-month volume
l4_steps.pain_point: Jet fuel crack spread volatility (2022: +180% YoY) can force hedge ratio outside approved bands requiring board escalation; no automated alert in OpenLink Endur

l4_steps.name: Submit annual fuel budget to Finance
l4_steps.input: Approved volume forecast, hedged price scenarios, prior-year actuals
l4_steps.output: Approved fuel OPEX budget by cost centre and quarter
l4_steps.kpi: Budget variance ≤±5% vs actual fuel cost at year-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Annual budget locked in Q4 but jet fuel prices move daily; SAP CO-PA budget version does not auto-update with market rate changes, causing stale variance reporting throughout the year

l4_steps.name: Evaluate and qualify fuel suppliers by station
l4_steps.input: Station list, ICAO airport codes, DEF STAN 91-091 quality standards, supplier capability submissions
l4_steps.output: Approved supplier register by airport with qualification status
l4_steps.kpi: ≥2 qualified suppliers at every Tier-1 hub; 100% supplier compliance with ASTM D1655 specification
l4_steps.pain_point: Remote and international stations frequently have a single into-plane agent with no qualified alternative; supply disruption at these stations forces flight hold with no automated contingency in SAP Ariba

l4_steps.name: Issue RFQ and evaluate competitive fuel bids
l4_steps.input: Volume forecast by station, approved supplier register, pricing reference (Platts Jet A)
l4_steps.output: Scored bid comparison matrix, recommended award by station
l4_steps.kpi: RFQ cycle time ≤21 calendar days; minimum 3 bids received per major hub station
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel suppliers submit non-standard pricing structures (flat-rate, index-linked, spot differential) making direct price comparison difficult; no normalisation tool in SAP Ariba Sourcing for jet fuel indices

l4_steps.name: Negotiate and execute fuel supply agreement
l4_steps.input: Bid comparison matrix, legal terms template, approved supplier, volume commitments
l4_steps.output: Signed fuel supply agreement (price formula, volume commitment, quality specs, liability caps)
l4_steps.kpi: Contract coverage ≥90% of annual volume; contract execution ≤30 days from award decision
l4_steps.pain_point: Into-plane agent contracts are separate from fuel supply contracts at most airports — coordinating two parallel contract cycles per station doubles procurement workload and creates liability gap periods

l4_steps.name: Generate daily fuel uplift orders from flight ops
l4_steps.input: Day-of flight plan (Jeppesen FliteDeck), fuel release quantities, tankering policy parameters
l4_steps.output: Fuel uplift orders by flight number and station for next 24 hours
l4_steps.kpi: Order accuracy ≥99.5% (uplift quantity within ±2% of flight plan requirement); order generation completed ≥4 hours before first departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Tankering decisions require real-time station price feed integration with FuelPlus; feed latency of 2–6 hours causes suboptimal tankering recommendations and missed cost-saving windows

l4_steps.name: Evaluate tankering opportunity vs payload penalty
l4_steps.input: Station fuel price differentials, aircraft weight/balance constraints (MTOW), cost-per-seat-mile model
l4_steps.output: Tankering go/no-go decision with estimated cost saving per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Tankering savings ≥$0.01/US gallon average across network; zero overweight departure events attributable to tankering
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing 737 MAX 8 MTOW constraints limit tankering payload trade-off on high-load routes; FuelPlus does not automatically model per-aircraft-variant weight limits, requiring manual override by dispatcher

l4_steps.name: Execute purchase order and payment authorisation
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba (Purchase Orders) + SAP S/4HANA Finance (AP)
l4_steps.input: Approved uplift orders, active supply contract reference, station fuel card limits
l4_steps.output: Confirmed PO, EFT payment instruction or fuel card charge authorisation
l4_steps.kpi: PO-to-supplier-confirmation cycle ≤4 hours for same-day uplifts; zero declined fuel card transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: International stations use Air BP or Shell Aviation fuel cards with daily spending limits that are frequently exceeded during irregular operations; no real-time limit monitoring integrated with SAP Ariba

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time fuel delivery at departure gate
l4_steps.input: Fuel truck arrival notification, loadsheet, flight plan fuel quantity (block fuel + reserve)
l4_steps.output: Uplift completion confirmation, fuel density and quantity record (litres and kg)
l4_steps.kpi: Fuelling completion ≥30 minutes before scheduled departure; zero misfuel incidents
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS delivery confirmations are occasionally lost or delayed at high-traffic hub stations; manual phone backup creates audit trail gaps that complicate invoice reconciliation and incident investigation

l4_steps.name: Validate fuel quality certificate at delivery
l4_steps.input: Fuel delivery note, batch certificate of analysis, DEF STAN 91-091 / ASTM D1655 spec sheet
l4_steps.output: Approved fuel release certificate or hold notice with reason code
l4_steps.kpi: 100% batch documentation compliance before uplift; zero fuel contamination incidents per year
l4_steps.pain_point: API gravity and water content test results take 2–4 hours at some stations — aircraft may be fuelled before final QC sign-off is recorded, creating regulatory exposure under EASA Part-M and FAA AC 43-12A

l4_steps.name: Manage fuel shortage or delivery failure exception
l4_steps.input: Shortage notification from into-plane agent, alternate supplier register, flight departure window
l4_steps.output: Emergency fuel order confirmation or flight departure hold decision with ATC notification
l4_steps.kpi: Shortage resolution ≤45 minutes; zero flight cancellations attributable to fuel unavailability
l4_steps.pain_point: At single-supplier airports there is no fallback into-plane agent; shortage forces a weight-limited departure or flight hold with no automated contingency order workflow in FuelPlus — manual station calls required

l4_steps.name: 3-way match fuel invoice to uplift and PO
l4_steps.input: Supplier invoice, FuelPlus uplift record, approved PO
l4_steps.output: Matched invoice cleared for payment or discrepancy flag with reason
l4_steps.kpi: Automated 3-way match rate ≥97%; discrepancy identification within 2 business days of invoice receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Into-plane agents invoice using different unit conventions (US gallons, litres, imperial gallons) with varying density references; unit conversion errors are the primary cause of auto-match failures and require manual correction

l4_steps.name: Resolve invoice discrepancy with fuel supplier
l4_steps.input: Discrepancy report, original supplier invoice, FuelPlus uplift records, PO
l4_steps.output: Approved credit note or revised invoice accepted into SAP FI-AP
l4_steps.kpi: Discrepancy recovery rate ≥95% within 30 days; average credit recovery ≥$0.005/gallon on disputed volume
l4_steps.pain_point: International suppliers dispute density conversion differences citing local regulatory standards — no standard IATA API gravity reference is integrated into the SAP Ariba supplier collaboration workflow, prolonging resolution cycles

l4_steps.name: Process approved fuel payment and post to GL
l4_steps.input: Approved invoice, contract payment terms, supplier bank details, FX daily rate
l4_steps.output: Payment run confirmation, GL posting to Fuel OPEX cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: On-time payment rate ≥98% per contract terms; zero duplicate payment incidents per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-currency fuel payments (USD, EUR, GBP, AED) require daily FX rate updates in SAP — rate feed lag of 1–2 days creates accounting timing differences vs actual bank settlement, generating reconciling items in period-end close

l4_steps.name: Mark-to-market hedge positions and test effectiveness
l4_steps.input: Platts jet fuel spot price, 12-month forward curve, open hedge position register
l4_steps.output: Daily MTM P&L report, hedge effectiveness ratio (prospective and retrospective)
l4_steps.kpi: Hedge effectiveness ≥80% (IFRS 9 hedge accounting qualification threshold); MTM report delivered by 09:00 each trading day
l4_steps.pain_point: IFRS 9 hedge accounting requires both prospective and retrospective effectiveness testing — OpenLink Endur configuration requires quarterly recertification by external auditor; any system upgrade risks de-qualifying existing hedges

l4_steps.name: Report fuel cost per ASM to senior leadership
l4_steps.input: Monthly uplift actuals (FuelPlus), invoice data (SAP FI-AP), hedge P&L (OpenLink), budget (SAP CO-PA)
l4_steps.output: Fuel cost per available seat mile (CASM) report, budget variance analysis, rolling 12-month forecast
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel CASM ≤$0.055; variance report published within 5 business days of month-end close
l4_steps.pain_point: Flight-level fuel cost attribution requires a data join between FuelPlus uplift records and SkyWORKS ASM data with no automated ETL pipeline — monthly manual extract and reconciliation takes 2–3 FTE days and introduces version control risk
